items.event_time_ist: Wednesday morning, Oct 21, 2026 (after the Aden strike; exact time undetermined)
items.source_name: NewsCord (6-outlet comparison, citing Al Jazeera and Yemeni media)
items.summary: Yemeni media reported that the Houthis targeted al-Rayyan Airport in al-Mukalla, capital of Hadhramaut, with four ballistic missiles on Wednesday morning, following their bombardment of Aden earlier the same day (Al Jazeera, cited by NewsCord's 6-outlet comparison). A government military source and a local official told Reuters the group also attacked 'Riyan airport' in the southeastern coastal city of Mukalla (Reuters via Devdiscourse). Sky News Arabia cited a Reuters reporter and an Aden police source saying the Houthis targeted the Mukalla airport with missiles and drones. No casualty or damage figures reported. This pushes the Wednesday-morning air campaign eastward to Hadhramaut — a new front beyond Aden.
items.title: Houthis fire ballistic missiles at al-Rayyan airport in Mukalla, eastern Yemen — campaign spreads to Hadhramaut

items.event_time_ist: Wednesday morning, Oct 21, 2026 (blast reported ~10:34 AM IST)
items.summary: Yemeni authorities said two missiles landed inside Aden International Airport's premises, about 500 meters from a Yemenia flight preparing to take off for Cairo; no human losses were recorded (via NewsCord's 6-outlet comparison). This adds official impact and casualty detail to Wednesday morning's already-reported Houthi ballistic-missile strike on the Aden airport area. Separately, Saree claimed the operation targeted the coalition's 'operations room' at Badr Camp in Aden with a ballistic missile; Sky News Arabia cited a Reuters reporter and Aden police source confirming the strike was Houthi-fired.
items.title: Two missiles fell inside Aden airport premises, ~500m from a Yemenia Cairo flight — no casualties
